title: Guardrail tuning + scorecard audit - POC sync with Northstar Medical
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latest scorecard results, investigate regression spikes, and agree guardrail adjustments. SE presented hypothesis for hallucination cluster tied to a prompt pattern; security raised SSO/KMS question. Agreed next steps: run targeted eval with trimmed prompt set, share latency/cost delta for dedicated vs hosted, and deliver updated guardrail rule set and playbook.
action_items: Ravi Patel: Produce per-model latency and cost delta CSV (hosted vs dedicated) — due 2025-11-18
Sofia Martinez: Supply the 1000 example prompts that hit the hallucination cluster — due 2025-11-15
Maya Chen: Share revised guardrail rule set and rollback playbook doc — due 2025-11-17
next_steps: Run targeted eval (trimmed prompt set) and return false-positive/false-negative counts
SE to test guardrail rule on canary branch and report latency impact
Schedule security deep dive for SSO/KMS integration next week (Jin + Redwood infra)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Grant (CSM); Dana Ruiz, Evan Brooks, Jin Park, Sofia Martinez (Northstar)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Weekly POC checkpoint focusing on quality regression, surface-level root cause analysis for hallucination cluster, and guardrail tuning.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. Um quick check, audio ok?
[00:06] Dana Ruiz: Yep, good here.
[00:08] Evan Brooks: All good.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: Ravi will walk through the latest scorecard, we'll triage the spike from last week, then discuss guardrail changes and security asks. Should be about 40 minutes.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: Ok jumping in, uh show of the heatmap — the high-level is that overall pass rate is stable at about 88 percent but we have this small cluster, uh the hallucination cluster, that spiked to 14% on Tuesday.
[00:35] Ravi Patel: timestamped examples are in the sheet under column E, but quick noise, these seem to be triggered when the prompt includes two short bulleted lists back-to-back. We suspect the KV cash — kv cash, i keep saying cash, the KV cache — interactions with prefix caching cause the model to drop context.
[00:52] Sofia Martinez: Is that the same behavior we saw in the synthetic tests? I thought the synthetic bench didn't surface it.
[00:57] Ravi Patel: Right, the synthetic batch we ran earlier didn't reproduce it because the real requests have those bulleted list separators and sometimes inline HTML. The synthetic generator doesn't add inline tags so the pattern was missed.
[01:15] Dana Ruiz: Can you show an example?
[01:18] (screen share noise)
[01:21] Ravi Patel: Sure, here: prompt id 8712 — question then two lists, model invents a medication name. You can see the token alignment shift at about token 84.
[01:33] Evan Brooks: Hmm, that medication hallucination is the thing our clinicians called out as high-risk. It's the main blocker for our pilot success metric.
[01:39] Maya Chen: Understood — thanks for flagging. A few paths: we can prune the prompt set to remove that pattern for now, add a guardrail rule to detect generated entities that are not on the whitelist, and also test small quantization change or kernel fallback which might stabilize attention.
[01:56] Jin Park: Quick security interjection — if we add a guardrail that checks against your internal medication list, we need to know how that list is stored/accessed. Are you suggesting Redwood will call Northstar APIs? We need SSO and KMS considerations.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Good question. The typical flow is Redwood hits a read-only reference call to a customer-hosted endpoint in your VPC via the private connector, or if you want we can ingest a snapshot into encrypted storage with KMS. We'll outline options and encryption at rest + audit log details in the security deep dive.
[02:28] Jin Park: Ok, please include retention windows and audit hooks in the doc.
[02:32] Ravi Patel: Back to the scorecard — we tried an interim guardrail yesterday that looked for unfamiliar entity patterns and forced the model to decline with a structured apology. That reduced hallucinations from 14% to about 6% but increased decline rate by 4% and added ~12ms median latency.
[02:52] Evan Brooks: 12ms is probably okay, but the decline rate is concerning because our UX team says too many declines will hurt adoption.
[03:01] Maya Chen: Totally. Another approach is to convert that guardrail to a soft flag: mark low-confidence outputs in metadata and route them for a light rerank or an L2 verification step, rather than outright decline. That preserves UX but gives you safety.
[03:15] Dana Ruiz: Can we get numbers on rerank cost?
[03:18] Ravi Patel: Yep, I'll add that. We'll show cost per 1k requests for rerank vs decline plus latency delta for both hosted and dedicated plans.
[03:27] Olivia Grant: I'll also pull historical traffic shape to see how often those bulleted list prompts occur — helps estimate total impact.
[03:34] Maya Chen: Great. Quick note on model variants — we saw that switching from the standard 7B to the quantized 7B-int8 reduced cost but slightly increased hallucination rate in that pattern. So the kernel selection and quantize-shun path matters.
[03:50] Evan Brooks: So are you suggesting we pin to standard float run for now?
[03:53] Ravi Patel: For the canary yes. We can run a split-test later with an A/B rollout and rollback policy in the console.
[03:59] Dana Ruiz: That leads to timeline — if we push a fix to the guardrail this week, how long until we can re-evaluate?
[04:04] Ravi Patel: If you supply the 1,000 example prompts by Friday, we can run targeted eval on Monday and have a results deck Tuesday. So two working days after we get the data.
[04:16] Sofia Martinez: We can do that, will export by EOD Friday.
[04:19] Jin Park: For the security deep dive, can we do SSO + KMS details next Wed? I need Ravi or someone from infra.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll schedule a 45-minute technical deep dive next Wednesday. We'll invite infra.
[04:29] (brief cross talk)
[04:32] Ravi Patel: Other small findings — there's an uptick in false positives on the toxicity catcher for non-English names; looks like the tokenization changes in the quantized runtime cause some ngram mismatch. So if you rely on the toxicity guardrail we should tune tokenizer normalization.
[04:48] Dana Ruiz: That's important for our global UX.
[04:50] Ravi Patel: Also ran the regression bisection; commit hash 6f3a9 had a new attention kernel, when we rolled that back locally the spike went away in 3/3 repros. So we want to avoid that kernel on production until we understand it.
[05:06] Evan Brooks: Can you label that kernel as opt-in for now?
[05:09] Ravi Patel: Yep, we'll mark that kernel behind a config flag; by default we'll stay on the older kernel for the pilot.
[05:15] Olivia Grant: I'll update the rollout plan in the project board.
[05:19] Maya Chen: Ok let's capture decisions: 1) Do not enable new attention kernel for pilot. 2) Implement soft-flag guardrail and canary test. 3) Customer to deliver example prompts. 4) Security deep dive next week.
[05:33] (long pause as notes are typed)
[05:38] Jin Park: Quick question on audit logs — does Redwood expose per-request logs with user obfuscation? We need to confirm PII handling.
[05:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide per-request metadata, and we support PII redaction and field-level encryption. We'll include the sample audit format in the security pack.
[05:55] Dana Ruiz: Ok good. On success criteria, we'll consider this a pass if hallucination rate in the flagged cluster drops below 3% and the overall decline or friction does not increase more than 2 percentage points.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Noted.
[06:09] (minute marker skip — meeting continues with more detail, interruptions and clarifications; audio artifacts and slight mistranscriptions present)
[20:12] Ravi Patel: Running the canary with soft flags increased median latency by about 18ms in the worst bucket, but 90th percentile stayed within SLA.
[20:28] Evan Brooks: The UX team will accept slightly higher median but not a huge increase in tail.
[20:33] Maya Chen: We'll include per-route 95th and 99th numbers in the next deck.
[27:05] Sophia Martinez: export is scheduled, sending via secure share.
[30:40] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: Ravi to produce latency/cost CSV; Maya to share guardrail doc; Sofia to send prompt dump; Redwood and Jin schedule security deep dive; SE to run targeted eval and report Tuesday. We'll reconvene same time next week for results.
[30:59] Dana Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[31:03] Evan Brooks: Thanks.
[31:05] Maya Chen: Thanks all, I'll follow up with calendar invites and notes.
[31:09] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: There are occasional mis-hears ("KV cash" for "KV cache", "quantize-shun" for "quantization") and some speaker overlap near the end.
